commands.review_summary:
Adds allow-always-unavailable reason metadata and propagates it through gateway protocol, exec hosts, approval renderers, plugin SDK reply helpers, Swift models, Control UI, and Matrix/Telegram/iMessage approval surfaces.

PR surface: Source +309, Tests +371, Other +4. Total +684 across 38 files.

Reproducibility: yes. Source inspection and the linked issue show current main removes Allow Always for one-shot commands and still has policy-only warning copy, but I did not live-run the prompt path in this read-only review.

target.title: fix #97069: [Bug]: Approval prompt wrongly says effective policy requires approval every time for non-persistable redirected command
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #97069.

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Exec approval prompts now explain why `Allow Always` is hidden for the current request. A redirected command such as `openclaw --version 2>&1` under `security=allowlist` / `ask=on-miss` is described as one-shot/non-persistable instead of incorrectly saying the effective policy requires approval every time.
- **Why it matters / User impact:** Users can distinguish a policy decision (`ask=always`) from a command-shape limitation. The prompt no longer suggests their approval policy changed when the command simply cannot be saved as a reusable allow-always approval.
- **Fix classification:** Minimal canonical root-cause fix for exec approval request metadata, prompt copy, and protocol/view surfaces.
- **Maintainer-ready confidence:** High for the approval behavior covered by the focused regression tests; macOS packaging-script coverage is left to remote macOS CI because local Windows Git Bash cannot execute that lane cleanly.
- **What did NOT change:** Approval policy evaluation, allowlist matching/storage, persistence pattern generation, command execution, approval expiry, reviewer routing, non-exec approvals, and actual approval decisions are not changed. This PR only carries and renders request-scoped unavailable-reason metadata.

## What Problem This Solves

Before this change, several approval prompt surfaces inferred the `Allow Always` explanation only from the missing `allow-always` decision. That made a non-persistable request look the same as an `ask=always` policy request.

For issue #97069, the policy is `security=allowlist` / `ask=on-miss`, but `openclaw --version 2>&1` is one-shot because shell redirection prevents a reusable approval pattern. The UI correctly hid `Allow Always`, but the explanatory text incorrectly blamed the effective policy. This PR carries a request-scoped unavailable reason so the same hidden action can render the correct explanation.

## Root Cause

- **Root cause:** The source-of-truth decision resolver could remove `allow-always` for both `ask=always` and one-shot/non-persistable commands, but downstream renderers only saw that `allow-always` was absent. They then reused the policy-only copy for all unavailable cases.
- **Why this is root-cause fix:** The canonical host/gateway request contract now records `allowedDecisions`, `unavailableDecisions`, and the derived `allowAlwaysUnavailableReason` together. Prompt renderers consume that source-of-truth metadata instead of guessing from a missing button, while schema validation and normalization keep older requests compatible when the explicit field is absent.
- **Architecture / source-of-truth check:** The canonical boundary remains request construction and validation, not individual UI strings. The gateway schema accepts the additive nullable reason, the server derives it from existing request fields, and renderers only map that normalized contract to copy. No migration, default policy, or persistence-store change is required.
- `ask=always` still wins over stale explicit reasons, so policy-required approval continues to use the policy explanation.
- `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]` under `ask=on-miss` now derives the one-shot explanation when an explicit reason is absent.

## Changes

- Added centralized exec approval copy/reason helpers for `policy-ask-always`, `one-shot-command`, and generic unavailable cases.
- Added request-scoped `allowAlwaysUnavailableReason` metadata and propagated it through:
  - gateway request creation and `exec.approval.get`
  - host/node approval registration and pending tool results
  - runtime, reply, forwarder, and embedded-agent approval prompts
  - approval view models and plugin reaction/manual fallback paths
  - native Matrix, Telegram, and iMessage approval surfaces
  - control UI parsing/rendering fallback
- Updated gateway protocol validation to accept known reason values or `null`, and regenerated the Swift protocol model.
- Added regression tests for request reason resolution, gateway validation, metadata propagation, policy-vs-one-shot copy, UI fallback behavior, and Matrix structured metadata.
- Public contract scope is additive and backward-compatible: older clients can omit the reason, send `null`, or rely on the server-derived fallback from `ask` and `unavailableDecisions`.
- Related open PR / same-contract scan was treated as background only; no related open PR was used to supersede or broaden this issue flow.
- Out of scope: changing approval policy semantics, adding new allowlist persistence patterns for redirected shell commands, changing command parsing, or changing non-exec/plugin approval behavior.

## Real behavior proof

- **Real environment tested:** Windows 10 Enterprise LTSC 2019 via Git Bash, Node v22.17.0, pnpm 11.2.2. The focused tests exercise the real prompt/reply/view-model builders used by gateway, runtime, UI, and chat/native approval paths.
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/exec-approval-unavailable-copy.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-approval-request.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-gateway.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-host-node.test.ts src/agents/bash-tools.exec-runtime.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/server-methods.test.ts src/infra/approval-view-model.test.ts src/infra/exec-approval-forwarder.test.ts src/infra/exec-approval-reply.test.ts src/plugin-sdk/approval-reaction-runtime.test.ts packages/gateway-protocol/src/exec-approvals-validators.test.ts ui/src/ui/controllers/exec-approval.test.ts ui/src/ui/views/exec-approval.test.ts extensions/matrix/src/approval-handler.runtime.test.ts
```

```text
node --import tsx scripts/protocol-gen-swift.ts
git diff --check
```

```text
OPENCLAW_CHECK_CHANGED_REMOTE_CHILD=1 OPENCLAW_CHANGED_LANES_RAW_SYNC=1 CI=1 PNPM_CONFIG_VERIFY_DEPS_BEFORE_RUN=false pnpm check:changed
```

- **Evidence after fix:** The focused approval regression run exited 0. Protocol generation exited 0 and rewrote the Swift model from the schema. `git diff --check` exited 0. The changed-file check passed the guard/typecheck/lint lanes before reaching the platform-specific macOS app CI lane.
- **Observed result after fix:** Regression assertions now verify that `ask=always` renders `The effective approval policy requires approval every time, so Allow Always is unavailable.`, while `ask=on-miss` with `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]` renders `Allow Always is unavailable because this command is one-shot and cannot be saved as a reusable approval.` The allowed replies/buttons omit `allow-always` in both unavailable cases.
- **What was not tested:** The `macOS app CI tests` lane did not complete successfully on this Windows Git Bash host. That lane was triggered by the generated Swift protocol model update under `apps/shared/OpenClawKit`; failures were in macOS packaging/signing script harness tests with Windows/Git Bash path-format differences and local Corepack/pnpm availability inside the harness. Remote macOS CI should provide authoritative coverage for that lane.

## Evidence

The focused approval regression command completed successfully with exit code 0.

The local changed-file command reported these lanes as passing before the macOS packaging-script lane:

```text
ok conflict markers
ok changelog attributions
ok guarded extension wildcard re-exports
ok plugin-sdk wildcard re-exports
ok duplicate scan target coverage
ok dependency pin guard
ok package patch guard
ok test temp creation report
ok typecheck core
ok typecheck core tests
ok typecheck extensions
ok typecheck extension tests
ok lint core
ok lint extensions
ok lint apps (swiftlint unavailable on this host)
failed: macOS app CI tests
```

The macOS app CI failures were local host/tooling failures in packaging/signing harness tests, not approval-flow assertion failures. Representative failure modes were path-format mismatches between Windows paths and Git Bash `/c/...` paths, plus Corepack/pnpm availability inside the spawned packaging harness.

## Regression Test Plan

- **Target test file:** `src/infra/exec-approval-unavailable-copy.test.ts` covers the new source-of-truth reason resolution. Additional regression coverage is in gateway, runtime, reply/forwarder, view-model, plugin reaction, UI controller/view, protocol validator, host registration, and Matrix approval handler tests.
- **Scenario locked in:** The regression scenario locks `ask=on-miss` plus `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]` for a redirected/non-persistable command shape and asserts the prompt offers only `allow-once|deny` with the one-shot copy. A separate policy scenario locks `ask=always` to the policy copy.
- **Why this is the smallest reliable guardrail:** The tests call the shared resolver, request registration, protocol validator, and prompt builders directly, so each source-of-truth and propagation boundary is covered without adding a brittle full end-to-end approval workflow fixture.
- Policy case: `ask=always` hides `Allow Always` and keeps the policy explanation.
- One-shot case: `ask=on-miss` plus `unavailableDecisions: ["allow-always"]` hides `Allow Always` and renders the one-shot/non-persistable explanation.
- Compatibility case: missing explicit reason is derived from existing request fields.
- Protocol case: schema accepts `policy-ask-always`, `one-shot-command`, `unavailable`, and `null`, while rejecting unknown reason strings.
- Surface propagation case: gateway, pending replies, native/chat approval metadata, and UI prompts preserve the unavailable metadata.

## Merge risk

- **Risk labels considered:** `merge-risk:contract`, `merge-risk:ui`, `merge-risk:extensions`, `merge-risk:generated-protocol`.
- **Risk explanation:** This is additive metadata, but it crosses public/wire-ish approval surfaces and generated protocol models. The main risk is a surface forgetting to forward the reason and falling back to generic/policy copy.
- **Why acceptable:** The gateway derives the reason from existing fields when explicit metadata is missing; `ask=always` takes precedence for safety; unknown reason strings normalize away; protocol validation allows `null` for compatibility; tests cover the affected prompt and metadata surfaces.
- **Patch quality notes:** Patch-quality warnings were reviewed. The added default returns are normalization exits for invalid/no metadata and for the valid case where `allow-always` is available; they do not mask a denial path. The fallback wording appears in regression tests that verify request fallback behavior. The public contract risk is bounded to an additive nullable schema field. The large diff is mostly propagation across existing approval surfaces so every renderer uses the same request-scoped source of truth instead of recreating policy guesses.
